Thesis.proseOnly: The thesis is the rate-vs-event argument and the Young-Daly-as-archetype claim; both are developed fully in prose.

The Price of Standing Still.proseOnly: Opening cost arithmetic ($340/min, $0.5M/day, 2.45 TB checkpoint) stays as prose; the numbers are single facts, not a system to diagram.

Failure Becomes a Rate.teaches: GPU-only MTBF collapse as fleet grows: 1 GPU at 50,000 h, 1,000 at 50 h, 10,000 at 5 h — with the full-system cascade (~3.9 h) and the Llama 3 measured point (~3.1 h at 16,384) plotted against the GPU-only line.
Failure Becomes a Rate.source: Book's fault_tolerance_mtbf_ladder margin figure + tbl-cluster-mtbf-scaling + the RSC/Llama-3 published rates.

Four Ways to Fail, One Invisible.proseOnly: The taxonomy is a four-row classification argument and the SDC cadence (~100 h, ~20/run) is arithmetic; the packet carries both as prose.

The Checkpoint Contract.teaches: The Young-Daly trade-off curve: save overhead falling hyperbolically, expected rework rising linearly, their shallow sum minimized near ~14 min at ~5.9% waste. The forgiving floor is the point.
The Checkpoint Contract.source: Book's fig-checkpoint-tradeoff: 175B example, 24.5 s write, 3.9 h MTBF, optimum ~13.8-14 min ~5.9%.

What Recovery Actually Buys.teaches: The ~6.6 min cold-restart budget as a stacked timeline: detect ~30 s, restart ~4 min, load ~24.5 s, warmup ~2 min — restart+warmup dominate, the I/O everyone fears is the small term.
What Recovery Actually Buys.source: Book's RecoveryBudget scenario (Gpt3RecoveryBudget1K/10K): t_total ~6.6 min, load ~24.5 s, daily loss 3 min @1K vs 31 min @10K.

Elastic and Stateless Recovery.teaches: The escalating detection stack: liveness probe -> heartbeat+timeout -> inference check -> progress-median straggler detection, each layer catching a class the one below misses, ending at the gray failure.
Elastic and Stateless Recovery.source: Book's detection mechanisms (health checks, 5 s/3-miss -> 12-17 s window, progress-median straggler flagging) + serving failover subsection.
